title: Jordan 2-0 Australia: Olwan's late strike punishes Popovic's 10 men
subtitle: Australia failed to build on their impressive showing against Qatar last time out, with Jordan dominating against them on Tuesday.
paragraphs: Ali Olwan's stoppage-time goal ensured Jordan finished on a high as they beat 10-man Australia 2-0 in an international friendly.

Mousa Al Tamari had given Jordan a first-half lead – moments after seeing a penalty saved – and after substitute Daniel Arzani was sent off for two bookable offences, Olwan made sure of the result in the 93rd minute.
Jordan immediately had Australia on the back foot, with Mahmoud Al Mardi and Al Tamari both testing Patrick Beach within the first four minutes.

Al Tamari also skewed over the crossbar as Jordan failed to make their early pressure count, but they were given a golden chance when Connor Metcalfe was penalised for a shove on the striker, who had skipped his way into the box.
It was a poor spot-kick down the middle from Al Tamari, who was denied by Beach's trailing right foot as he dived to his left in the 32nd minute, but Jordan soon found their opener.
Amer Jamous played it long down the right, and Al Tamari latched onto it, cut inside and drilled a low finish in at the near post just two minutes after his penalty miss.

Australia failed to improve after the break, and Tony Popovic's side had to play the last 10 minutes with 10 men after Arzani received two quickfire bookings. His first was for a tug on Al Tamari before he received his marching orders when he clipped the back of Adballah Nasib.
Jordan thought they had doubled their lead in the 92nd minute when Odeh Fakhoury raced in behind before coolly slotting past Beach, who had rushed out, but the offside flag denied him.
But it was Olwan who got them over the line after a long ball over the top caused chaos. Ghaith Al Madadha held off the pressure well before picking out Olwan to slide it into the bottom-left corner.
Jordan blow away Popovic's lacklustre side
Australia impressed in their 3-0 victory over Qatar last time out, with a dominant first half seeing them score all three goals to get back to winning ways.
However, they struggled to lay a glove on Jordan at Suheim Bin Hamad Stadium as they mustered just 0.14 expected goals (xG) from seven shots, though only one was on target.

Jordan, by contrast, had 13 attempts, with seven of those on target, and Al Tamari was the catalyst for their win, having six of their total shots. He also had eight touches in the opposition box, as many as Australia managed combined.

Al Tamari netted his 26th international goal, moving joint-fifth in Jordan's all-time scorers. He could have had more, too, but Beach denied him from 12 yards, becoming the first Australian goalkeeper to save a penalty since Mat Ryan in June 2025 against Saudi Arabia.
Arzani could have few complaints about either of his bookings, becoming the first Socceroo to be dismissed in a friendly match since Mitchell Langerak against Ecuador in March 2024.
This marks just the second time Australia have lost by more than one goal against Jordan, also losing 2-0 in October 2015, and it leaves Popovic with work to do.
